note: Live-session recording of the screen scenes (series/tools/rec). prepare/teardown run on the laptop, not recorded; commands are typed and run for real. The episode is copied to a neutral folder C:\lab\plNN so no user name shows in paths.
prepare: # owner allows the Windows firewall prompt for node.exe (127.0.0.1) once, off camera: run 'node src/cli.js serve' briefly in the copy if needed

screens.name: timings
prepare: if (Test-Path C:\lab\pl09\server.pid) { Stop-Process -Id (Get-Content C:\lab\pl09\server.pid) -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Remove-Item C:\lab\pl09\server.pid }

$p = Start-Process node -ArgumentList 'src/cli.js', 'serve', '--port', '5090', '--latency', '300', '--fail-first', 'operations' -WorkingDirectory C:\lab\pl09 -RedirectStandardOutput C:\lab\pl09\api.log -RedirectStandardError C:\lab\pl09\api.err -WindowStyle Hidden -PassThru; $p.Id | Set-Content C:\lab\pl09\server.pid; Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
screens.note: The approvals service runs as a hidden background process (node src/cli.js serve --port 5090 --latency 300 --fail-first operations); its real log is shown with Get-Content api.log instead of a left pane.

steps: Left pane: cd C:\lab\pl09; node src/cli.js serve --port 5090 --latency 1000 --fail-first operations
Right pane: cd C:\lab\pl09; node src/cli.js intake samples/requests.csv --concurrency 5 --no-cache
Press Ctrl+C in the right pane after about half a second
Frame both panes: five 'ABORTED by the client' lines on the left; stop the server with Ctrl+C
mask: window and tab titles; short prompt: function prompt { '> ' } in both panes
